q: Heavy metals are metals with high density and toxic effects even at very low ____.
e: Heavy metals are metals with high density and toxic effects even at very low concentrations. Concentrations is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Pure arsenic is rarely found in nature and is not very toxic, but it can be oxidised easily in humid air and becomes toxic by conversion to arsenic ____.
e: Pure arsenic is rarely found in nature and is not very toxic, but it can be oxidised easily in humid air and becomes toxic by conversion to arsenic anhydride. Anhydride is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Arsenic is mostly found in the form of +3 and +5 oxidation states but is not in ____ form in nature.
e: Arsenic is mostly found in the form of +3 and +5 oxidation states but is not in elemental form in nature. Oxidation state tracks how oxidised an atom is; transition metals often show several values.

q: The desorption and dissolution of arsenic from arsenic rich rocks and minerals are the main sources of groundwater contamination and ____.
e: The desorption and dissolution of arsenic from arsenic rich rocks and minerals are the main sources of groundwater contamination and soil. Soil is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Compounds such as calcium arsenide, lead arsenide and sodium arsenate are used for the production of paint, glass, ceramics, and ____.
e: Compounds such as calcium arsenide, lead arsenide and sodium arsenate are used for the production of paint, glass, ceramics, and semiconductors. Semiconductors is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Sodium arsenate is used to kill some parasites in fruit cultivation and ____ growing.
e: Sodium arsenate is used to kill some parasites in fruit cultivation and potato growing. Potato is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Cadmium is released into the atmosphere predominantly as elemental cadmium and cadmium ____.
e: Cadmium is released into the atmosphere predominantly as elemental cadmium and cadmium oxide. Oxide is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Tobacco ____ is also a significant source of cadmium exposure.
e: Tobacco smoking is also a significant source of cadmium exposure. Smoking is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Various salts of cadmium are commonly used in electronic cells, accumulators, porcelain, nuclear materials, amalgam in dentistry, plastic, metal coating, vacuum tubes, and ____ materials.
e: Various salts of cadmium are commonly used in electronic cells, accumulators, porcelain, nuclear materials, amalgam in dentistry, plastic, metal coating, vacuum tubes, and photovoltaic materials. Photovoltaic is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Lead enters the atmosphere largely in the exhaust fumes from internal combustion ____.
e: Lead enters the atmosphere largely in the exhaust fumes from internal combustion engines. Engines is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The primary use of lead is in the manufacture of batteries, and in the production of paint, alloys and metal products in the ____.
e: The primary use of lead is in the manufacture of batteries, and in the production of paint, alloys and metal products in the industry. Industry is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: An increased level of lead in the environment can result in decreased growth and reproduction in plants and animals, and ____ effects in vertebrates.
e: An increased level of lead in the environment can result in decreased growth and reproduction in plants and animals, and neurological effects in vertebrates. Neurological is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Inorganic mercury can be transformed into methylmercury by microorganisms such as phytoplanktons and ____.
e: Inorganic mercury can be transformed into methylmercury by microorganisms such as phytoplanktons and fungi. Fungi is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Methylmercury then ____ in fish and shellfish.
e: Methylmercury then bioaccumulates in fish and shellfish. Bioaccumulates is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The source of exposure to low levels is mercury released from amalgam from the panning of gold and fillings in ____.
e: The source of exposure to low levels is mercury released from amalgam from the panning of gold and fillings in teeth. Teeth is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Mercury may have toxic effects on the nervous, digestive and immune systems, and on the lungs, kidneys, skin, eyes, and development of the child in utero and early in ____.
e: Mercury may have toxic effects on the nervous, digestive and immune systems, and on the lungs, kidneys, skin, eyes, and development of the child in utero and early in life. Life is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: A pesticide is a substance that kills a pest, or it prevents or reduces the damage a pest may ____.
e: A pesticide is a substance that kills a pest, or it prevents or reduces the damage a pest may cause. Cause is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Some common pesticide families include organophosphates, organochlorines, carbamates and thiocarbamates, and ____.
e: Some common pesticide families include organophosphates, organochlorines, carbamates and thiocarbamates, and pyrethroids. Pyrethroids is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Adsorption occurs because of the attraction between a chemical and soil ____.
e: Adsorption occurs because of the attraction between a chemical and soil particles. Particles is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Positively charged pesticide molecules are attracted to and can bind to negatively charged ____ particles.
e: Positively charged pesticide molecules are attracted to and can bind to negatively charged clay particles. Clay is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The transfer includes processes that move the pesticide away from the target site, such as volatilisation, spray drift, runoff, leaching, absorption and crop ____.
e: The transfer includes processes that move the pesticide away from the target site, such as volatilisation, spray drift, runoff, leaching, absorption and crop removal. Removal is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Degradation is the process of pesticide breakdown after ____.
e: Degradation is the process of pesticide breakdown after application. Application is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Pesticides are broken down by microbes, chemical reactions, and ____.
e: Pesticides are broken down by microbes, chemical reactions, and photodegradation. Photodegradation is breakdown caused by sunlight.

q: Persistent organic pollutants (POPs) and volatile organic compounds (VOCs) are two of the most insidious forms of toxic ____.
e: Persistent organic pollutants (POPs) and volatile organic compounds (VOCs) are two of the most insidious forms of toxic contamination. Volatile organic compounds evaporate easily and can pollute air.

q: POPs are carbon-based organic compounds that have the special abilities to be long-lasting and to resist breakdown into safer ____.
e: POPs are carbon-based organic compounds that have the special abilities to be long-lasting and to resist breakdown into safer substances. Persistent organic pollutants last a long time in the environment because they resist breakdown.

q: POPs include industrial chemicals like polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) and pesticides like dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane (____).
e: POPs include industrial chemicals like polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) and pesticides like dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane (DDT). Persistent organic pollutants last a long time in the environment because they resist breakdown.

q: POPs are chemically stable, remain intact in the environment for long periods, and are ____ in nature.
e: POPs are chemically stable, remain intact in the environment for long periods, and are lipophilic in nature. Persistent organic pollutants last a long time in the environment because they resist breakdown.

q: Therefore, POPs accumulate in the fatty tissue of living organisms and reside for a longer period of time finally affecting humans and ____.
e: Therefore, POPs accumulate in the fatty tissue of living organisms and reside for a longer period of time finally affecting humans and wildlife. Persistent organic pollutants last a long time in the environment because they resist breakdown.

q: VOCs are organic chemicals that pollute the air and be absorbed or inhaled by humans, animals and ____.
e: VOCs are organic chemicals that pollute the air and be absorbed or inhaled by humans, animals and plants. Volatile organic compounds evaporate easily and can pollute air.

q: Under sunlight, VOCs react with nitrogen oxides emitted mainly from vehicles, power plants and industrial activities to form ____.
e: Under sunlight, VOCs react with nitrogen oxides emitted mainly from vehicles, power plants and industrial activities to form ozone. Volatile organic compounds evaporate easily and can pollute air.

q: The accumulation of ozone, fine particulates and other gaseous pollutants results in smog that reduces ____.
e: The accumulation of ozone, fine particulates and other gaseous pollutants results in smog that reduces visibility. Visibility is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The burning of plastics releases toxic gases like dioxins, furans, mercury and polychlorinated biphenyls into the ____.
e: The burning of plastics releases toxic gases like dioxins, furans, mercury and polychlorinated biphenyls into the atmosphere. Atmosphere is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.
